T14.title: Fixed-k paired comparison of the dedicated and shared rules by cell category
rows: shared rule at a fixed stock
shared rule with a different allocation order
notes: Cell counts over 96 fixed-k cells in total, at tolerance 5% on three service rates (capacity-only unmet, EV parking failure, ICEV parking failure).
k is selected on seeds 1-4 under the dedicated rule and evaluated on seeds 5-10; the two seed sets are disjoint.
A cell counts as feasible only when every rate is valid and at or below the tolerance; a rate with a zero denominator is not applicable and does not make a cell feasible on its own.
Only the 'shared only' column would evidence that shared use substitutes for equipment; it is zero in both rows.

T15.title: Three minimal traces in which one extra equipped bay lowers ICEV parking failures
notes: Counts are failures per trace over the whole operating window; the trace is replayed at every k and the numbers agree with the mechanism model in all k, not only at the two shown.

Column 6 repeats the same trace with the fallback of an EV to an ordinary bay removed; the decrease in column 3 disappears in all three traces, as it does under a reversed bay order and under dwell times shortened by 20%.
Traces are synthetic configurations of the mechanism model, not field measurements of a site.

T16.title: Smallest admissible integer count under the two information conditions
notes: k values are the smallest count at which the three service rates are at or below 5% in that unit; k is searched over the complete integer grid 0-40.
Categories are read at the k of the I0 unit: both means feasible under both conditions, only-I0 means feasible under I0 alone.

Across 8 paired units the change is negative in 8, zero in 0 and positive in 0 (median -9.5, range -17 to -2); across 328 fixed-k comparisons the categories are both 143, only I0 26, only I1 61, neither 98.
The I1 policy is a heuristic, so the table compares two implemented policies and not two optima.

T17.title: Feasible sets of the two rules over complete integer grids
notes: Pairs are lot-seed groups compared at tolerance 5% over the complete grid k = 0-40; rule A is the dedicated rule, so the second rule is the shared one in every row.

Columns: first only = admissible under the first rule only; restored = admissible under the second rule only; smaller k = the second rule attains a strictly smaller minimal count; disjoint = both rules admissible but the sets share no k.

Set shape over 660 groups: broken sets 0, empty under the inclusive convention 124, empty under the strict convention 139, groups where the two conventions differ 15, sets truncated at the grid edge 437.
Aggregated over the same pairs, service at a common k improves under the second rule in 4 pairs and worsens in 6.
A set truncated at the grid edge is not evidence that no larger admissible count exists.
